findings.property: Preserve the existing general regular/special path argument checks while recognizing literal arguments after an interpreter script (program-input-repair-plan-v2.md, contract 2).
findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py:239-252 replaces the prior unconditional lstat argument loop with values = argv[1:] if script_index is None else argv[1:1]. For every recognized Python or Bash script, argv[1:1] is empty. The earlier loop at 225-230 only checks os.path.isfile, so it ignores FIFOs, devices, sockets and dangling symlinks. Therefore an otherwise healthy pinned resolved Python -I -S SCRIPT /absolute/input.fifo, or Bash -p SCRIPT /absolute/input.fifo, is admitted despite the explicit nonregular input and absent pin. The pinned script could read that unpinned stream; even a harmless script that only writes its marker would demonstrate prohibited admission. DEVNULL protects fd 0, not this explicit argument. The v2-to-v3 diff establishes this as a removed check, not a request for arbitrary dependency discovery. The existing FIFO-script regression covers the script position only, and the literal-argument table has no special-file argument case.
findings.uncertainty: Confirmed by complete admission-path source analysis and the v2-to-v3 diff. No extra behavioral probe was run because only the supplied suite was authorized. This is a scoped contract regression; it is not a claim of containment bypass against an untrusted arbitrary approved script.
findings.falsifier: In any authorized repair, first preserve an actual behavioral RED against v3 using a valid supported pinned Python -I -S script and an existing FIFO as a later argument, then the equivalent Bash -p case. Require exit 78 before journal mutation or the harmless script marker. Preserve the existing healthy literal -m/-/-c argument controls and pinned regular-input controls. Restore special-path checking for actual script arguments without treating those literal flags as interpreter source modes; no generic parser/framework is needed.
